cs.t: Ah memories... and my personal progress over time: My very first calculator: [0] My first slide rule: [1] (for two years or so, then we switched to electronic calculators) Before I could afford a computer I spent a a few years on computers I didn't own, ZX Spectrum, C64, C128, 8bit Atari, KC85/1,2,3, but also LC 80 [2] My 1st (own) computer: East German 8 bit KC85/4 with the CAOS operating system (the makers had a good sense of humor, it means "Cassette-Aided OS") [3][4]. Mass-storage was ones regular stereo cassette radio recorder, a floppy disc drive was available but rare. My 2nd computer: Atari 1040 STFM [5] - bought with my first West German money after reunification! Finally 16 bit! Atari ST software worth mentioning: "Script 2" was a wonderful word processor for Atari [6]. When used in combination with the (for the time) excellent black/white monitor and a 24 needle printer (Epson LQ 580) I got near laser printer quality through the special drivers of that program. Worst Atari incident: I had a capacitor (literally) blow up on me with a very loud  BANG! . I'll end with the Atari. The next one - for my studies - was a 486DX33 8MB RAM machine with Windows 3.1, soon RedHat Linux (1995). Thanks to the student network I could start large programs like Netscape on another student's Pentium PC (in another building) and export the display until I was able to upgrade to 16 MB RAM... and all the usual mid-1990s Unix systems, also available remotely thanks to the network.
